Mszczonow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mszczonów, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Mszczonów in the 17th century, though an organized community only formed in the following century's second half; the town later became seat of the Amshinov Hasidic dynasty and birthplace of writer and MP Hirsz Dawid Nomberg. Jewish population peaked at 5,106 (64% of the town) in 1910, still numbering 2,188 by 1921, before deportation to the Warsaw Ghetto in 1941 and murder at Treblinka the following year. The cemetery was established in 1763 on a square plot originally measuring '70 x 70 ells,' later expanded to roughly 103-133 metres per side by 1927. Formally closed to burials in 1964, part of its land was later separated and partially built over. About a hundred tombstones survive, the oldest dating to 1772-1791; two rebuilt ohels honor Rebbe Jakow Dawid (d. 1877) and dayan Aharon ha-Kohen (d. 1873), restoration work commissioned by the Singer and Boim families alongside the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage.
